name: Essential Hypertension
overview: Meta-analysis confirms lowering SBP by 10 mmHg reduces major cardiovascular events by 20%, stroke by 27%, and heart failure by 28%. First-line pharmacological classes (thiazide diuretics, CCBs, ACEi/ARBs) demonstrate equivalent mortality reduction; CCBs excel in stroke prevention (RR 0.82), while ACEi/ARBs offer superior renal protection in diabetic cohorts (HR 0.68).
patient_plain_language: Blood pressure is the force of blood pushing against the walls of your arteries. When it stays high, it slowly damages your blood vessels like running water at too high a pressure through household pipes.

symptoms.name: Occipital morning headache
symptoms.description: Dull ache at the base of the skull upon waking, often resolving after several hours.

symptoms.name: Dizziness / Lightheadedness
symptoms.description: Transient unsteadiness, particularly upon standing or rapid posture changes.

symptoms.name: Facial flushing
symptoms.description: Warmth and erythema of cheeks and neck during acute blood pressure surges.

symptoms.name: Blurred vision
symptoms.description: Intermittent visual haziness during hypertensive spikes due to retinal vascular tone changes.

symptoms.name: Epistaxis (Nosebleeds)
symptoms.description: Spontaneous bleeding from fragile nasal mucosal vessels under high vascular pressure.

symptoms.name: Asymptomatic elevation
symptoms.description: Often completely silent ('silent killer') with no overt warning signs until target-organ damage occurs.

red_flags: Systolic BP > 180 mmHg or diastolic > 120 mmHg accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, or vision changes (Hypertensive Emergency)

solutions.name: Thiazide Diuretics (Chlorthalidone / Hydrochlorothiazide)
solutions.description: Inhibits sodium and chloride reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule, reducing extracellular fluid volume and peripheral vascular resistance.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Chlorthalidone 12.5–25 mg orally once daily in the morning; or HCTZ 25–50 mg once daily.
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min for HCTZ)
solutions.monitoring: Basic metabolic panel (BMP) checking serum potassium, sodium, and creatinine at 2–4 weeks.

solutions.name: ACE Inhibitors (Lisinopril / Enalapril) or ARBs (Losartan / Valsartan)
solutions.description: Blocks renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), preventing angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone release. Preferred in diabetes or CKD with proteinuria.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Lisinopril 10–40 mg once daily; or Losartan 50–100 mg once daily.
solutions.monitoring: Serum creatinine and potassium 2–4 weeks post-initiation; hold if potassium >5.5 mEq/L.

solutions.name: Dihydropyridine Calcium Channel Blockers (Amlodipine)
solutions.description: Inhibits L-type calcium channels on vascular smooth muscle cells, causing potent peripheral arterial vasodilation and afterload reduction.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Amlodipine 2.5–10 mg orally once daily.
solutions.monitoring: Assess lower extremity edema at routine follow-up.

solutions.name: DASH Nutritional Pattern & Dietary Sodium Reduction
solutions.description: Diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy with reduced saturated fat and cholesterol. Restrict sodium to <1,500 mg/day (or at least 1,000 mg/day reduction).
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Daily dietary adherence yields ~11 mmHg SBP reduction in hypertensive adults; 90–150 min/week moderate aerobic exercise.
solutions.monitoring: Standardized home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) 2 morning and 2 evening readings for 7 days.

name: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF)
alternative_names: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF)
overview: In 8,442 patients with HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%), Sacubitril/Valsartan reduced composite CV death or heart failure hospitalization by 20% compared to Enalapril (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.73-0.87; p<0.001). All-cause mortality was reduced by 16% (p<0.001). Guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) establishes foundational four-pillar therapy: ARNI/ACEi, beta-blockers, MRA, and SGLT2i.
patient_plain_language: Heart failure means your heart muscle is pumping less efficiently than normal, making it harder to supply oxygen to your organs. It does not mean your heart has stopped beating.

symptoms.name: Dyspnea on exertion
symptoms.description: Breathlessness during physical effort due to pulmonary venous congestion and inadequate cardiac output reserve.

symptoms.name: Orthopnea
symptoms.description: Inability to lie flat without progressive breathlessness; requires 2 or more pillows for sleep.

symptoms.name: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (PND)
symptoms.description: Waking from sleep gasping for air 1–2 hours after recumbency as peripheral edema fluid re-enters circulatory volume.

symptoms.name: Bilateral lower extremity edema
symptoms.description: Dependent pitting edema around ankles and pretibial areas from systemic venous hypertension.

symptoms.name: Fatigue and weakness
symptoms.description: Profound generalized physical exhaustion due to low forward systemic perfusion.

symptoms.name: Nocturnal dry cough
symptoms.description: Persistent dry wheezing cough when recumbent due to pulmonary capillary engorgement.

red_flags: Weight gain >2-3 lbs in 24 hours or 5 lbs in one week
Inability to lie flat without severe air hunger (orthopnea)
Pink frothy sputum

solutions.name: ARNI (Sacubitril/Valsartan - Entresto)
solutions.description: Neprilysin inhibitor combined with angiotensin receptor blocker. Enhances natriuretic peptide system while inhibiting RAAS. Foundational Pillar 1 of GDMT.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Initial 49/51 mg PO BID (or 24/26 mg BID if low baseline BP/eGFR), titrating every 2–4 weeks to target 97/103 mg PO BID.
contraindications: Concurrent ACE inhibitor within 36 hours (angioedema risk)
solutions.monitoring: Blood pressure, serum potassium, and renal function (eGFR) at 1–2 weeks following initiation.

solutions.name: Evidence-Based Beta-Blockers (Carvedilol / Metoprolol Succinate / Bisoprolol)
solutions.description: Blunts chronic toxic sympathetic overactivation, reverses LV remodeling, reduces heart rate, and lowers sudden cardiac death. Foundational Pillar 2.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Carvedilol starting 3.125 mg BID, doubling every 2 weeks to target 25–50 mg BID; or Metoprolol Succinate ER 25–200 mg daily.
contraindications: Acute decompensated heart failure with overt fluid overload
solutions.monitoring: Heart rate (target resting 60–70 bpm) and daily morning weights.

solutions.name: Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists (Spironolactone / Eplerenone)
solutions.description: Blocks aldosterone binding at renal and cardiovascular receptors, reducing myocardial fibrosis and potassium wasting. Foundational Pillar 3.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Spironolactone 12.5–25 mg daily, titrating to 50 mg daily as tolerated.
solutions.monitoring: Check potassium and creatinine at 1, 4, and 12 weeks, then semi-annually.

solutions.name: SGLT2 Inhibitors (Dapagliflozin / Empagliflozin)
solutions.description: Promotes osmotic diuresis, improves myocardial energetics, and lowers cardiac preload and afterload independent of diabetes status. Foundational Pillar 4.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily; or Empagliflozin 10 mg once daily.
contraindications: Type 1 diabetes without specialist protocol (euglycemic DKA risk)
solutions.monitoring: Volume status and glycemic parameters if co-administered with sulfonylureas/insulin.

name: Atrial Fibrillation & Stroke Prophylaxis
overview: Apixaban was superior to Warfarin in preventing stroke or systemic embolism (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.66-0.95; p=0.01 for superiority) with a 31% reduction in major bleeding (HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.60-0.80; p<0.001) and a significant reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.89; p=0.047). ACC/AHA guidelines strongly recommend DOACs over vitamin K antagonists in non-valvular AF.
patient_plain_language: Atrial fibrillation is an irregular, quivering heartbeat in the top chambers of your heart. Because blood does not pump out smoothly, it can pool and form clots that travel to the brain, causing a stroke.

symptoms.name: Palpitations / Fluttering heartbeat
symptoms.description: Irregular, rapid sensation of skipping beats or fluttering in the chest.

symptoms.name: Exertional dyspnea
symptoms.description: Shortness of breath with minimal activity due to loss of atrial kick and rapid ventricular response.

symptoms.name: Lightheadedness / Dizziness
symptoms.description: Cerebral hypoperfusion during rapid ventricular rates or sudden pauses.

symptoms.name: Exercise intolerance
symptoms.description: Substantial decrease in physical stamina and early onset exhaustion.

symptoms.name: Chest tightness
symptoms.description: Discomfort resulting from increased myocardial oxygen demand during tachyarrhythmia.

red_flags: Sudden facial droop, arm weakness, or speech slurring (FAST criteria for stroke)
Uncontrolled bleeding from minor cuts, coughing up blood, or black tarry stools

solutions.name: Direct Oral Anticoagulants - DOACs (Apixaban / Rivaroxaban / Dabigatran)
solutions.description: Directly inhibits factor Xa or thrombin, preventing left atrial appendage thrombus formation and ischemic stroke.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Apixaban 5 mg orally BID (reduce to 2.5 mg BID if any 2 of: age ≥80, body weight ≤60 kg, serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL).
solutions.monitoring: Annual renal function (CrCl via Cockcroft-Gault) and CBC.

solutions.name: Rate Control Therapy (Metoprolol Succinate / Diltiazem)
solutions.description: AV nodal blocking agents to control ventricular rate at rest (<80–110 bpm) and during exertion.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Metoprolol succinate 25–100 mg daily; or Diltiazem CD 120–360 mg daily (avoid diltiazem in HFrEF).
solutions.monitoring: Resting and exertional heart rate on ECG or telemetry.

name: Hypercholesterolemia & Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD)
overview: Extensive meta-analyses of Cholesterol Treatment Trialists (CTT) show a 21% reduction in major vascular events per 1.0 mmol/L (~39 mg/dL) reduction in LDL-C. High-intensity statin therapy reduces LDL-C by ≥50%, moderate-intensity by 30-49%. Addition of non-statins (Ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors) yields proportional additional cardiovascular event risk reductions.
patient_plain_language: Cholesterol is a fatty substance your body needs, but too much 'bad' LDL cholesterol builds up inside your artery walls like rust in pipes, narrowing the pathway for blood to flow.

name: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) & Pulmonary Embolism (PE)
overview: CHEST guidelines strongly recommend DOACs (Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, Dabigatran, Edoxaban) over Vitamin K antagonists for initial and long-term VTE management in non-cancer patients (Grade 1B). Minimum treatment duration for provoked VTE is 3 months; extended unprovoked VTE anticoagulation carries a >80% relative risk reduction in recurrent thrombosis.
patient_plain_language: A DVT is a blood clot that forms in the deep veins of your leg. If part of the clot breaks free and travels to the lungs, it is called a pulmonary embolism (PE), which is a serious medical emergency.

name: Stable Ischemic Heart Disease & Angina

name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
overview: Targeted HbA1c control (<7.0% for most non-pregnant adults) significantly reduces microvascular complications (retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy). For individuals with established ASCVD, heart failure, or CKD, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists confer organ-protective benefits independent of baseline HbA1c or background metformin use (UKPDS, EMPA-REG, LEADER).
patient_plain_language: In type 2 diabetes, your body’s cells become resistant to insulin—the key that lets sugar enter your cells for energy. Because the lock doesn't work, sugar builds up in your bloodstream.

symptoms.name: Polyuria (Frequent urination)
symptoms.description: Excessive urination due to osmotic diuresis when blood glucose exceeds renal threshold (~180 mg/dL).

symptoms.name: Polydipsia (Excessive thirst)
symptoms.description: Persistent severe thirst triggered by hypothalamic dehydration signaling.

symptoms.name: Polyphagia (Extreme hunger)
symptoms.description: Intense hunger despite eating, as glucose is blocked from entering cells due to insulin resistance.

symptoms.name: Unexplained weight loss
symptoms.description: Loss of body mass as catabolism breaks down glycogen, fat, and muscle stores.

symptoms.name: Blurred vision
symptoms.description: Osmotic swelling of ocular lens during periods of acute hyperglycemia.

symptoms.name: Peripheral numbness / Tingling (Paresthesias)
symptoms.description: Distal symmetric stocking-glove sensory loss from chronic diabetic microvascular neuropathy.

red_flags: Blood glucose >250 mg/dL with nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and rapid deep breathing (Diabetic Ketoacidosis / HHS)
Blood glucose <70 mg/dL with confusion, sweating, shakiness, or loss of consciousness

solutions.name: Metformin Extended-Release (Biguanide)
solutions.description: Activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), reducing hepatic gluconeogenesis and improving peripheral insulin sensitivity.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: 500 mg orally once daily with evening meal, titrating by 500 mg weekly to target 2,000 mg daily in divided doses.
contraindications: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m² (Black Box Warning: Lactic Acidosis)
side_effects: Vitamin B12 deficiency with long-term use
solutions.monitoring: Annual eGFR and serum vitamin B12 levels.

solutions.name: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Semaglutide / Dulaglutide)
solutions.description: Enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, slows gastric emptying, and reduces MACE and progression of CKD.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Semaglutide SubQ 0.25 mg weekly x 4 weeks, escalate to 0.5 mg weekly; may increase to 1.0–2.0 mg weekly based on glycemic goals.
contraindications: Personal/family history of Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma (MTC)
solutions.monitoring: HbA1c quarterly until stable, then semi-annually.

solutions.name: SGLT2 Inhibitors (Empagliflozin / Dapagliflozin)
solutions.description: Inhibits sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 in proximal renal tubules, inducing urinary glucose excretion and providing substantial cardiovascular/renal protection.
solutions.dosage_or_protocol: Empagliflozin 10–25 mg orally once daily in the morning.
solutions.monitoring: Renal function and skin integrity of feet.

overview: In 2,539 adults with obesity, Tirzepatide (dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist) at 15 mg weekly achieved a mean weight reduction of 20.9% (-23.6 kg) at 72 weeks compared to 3.1% in placebo (p<0.001). Over 91% of participants in the 15 mg cohort achieved ≥5% weight loss, accompanied by significant reductions in blood pressure, fasting insulin, and lipid parameters.
patient_plain_language: Obesity is a complex, chronic biological condition where appetite hormones and metabolism make it difficult to maintain a lower body weight, not simply a matter of willpower.

name: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH / NASH)
overview: In 966 patients with biopsy-proven MASH and fibrosis stages F1B-F3, Resmetirom (thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist) achieved MASH resolution with no worsening of fibrosis in 29.9% (100 mg) vs. 9.7% (placebo) (p<0.001), and fibrosis improvement of at least one stage with no worsening of NAFLD activity score in 25.9% vs. 14.2% (p<0.001).
patient_plain_language: MASH is an advanced form of fatty liver where excess fat stored in liver cells causes inflammation and scarring (fibrosis), similar to how skin forms a scar after an injury.

symptoms.name: Bloating and abdominal distension
symptoms.description: Visible fullness or discomfort after meals. Characteristically observed in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis (MASH / NASH).

symptoms.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding (Melena/Hematochezia)

red_flags: Yellowing of the eyes or skin (jaundice)
Abdominal swelling (ascites), confusion, or vomiting blood

name: Primary Hypothyroidism
overview: Guidelines establish Levothyroxine monotherapy as standard of care. Full replacement dose is approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day in healthy adults, with lower initiation doses (25-50 mcg) in elderly patients or those with coronary artery disease to avoid precipitating cardiac ischemia. Routine addition of Liothyronine (T3) is not recommended by consensus due to lack of sustained RCT benefit.
patient_plain_language: Your thyroid gland in your neck produces hormones that set your body's metabolic speed. In hypothyroidism, the gland is underactive, causing your body's engines to slow down.

name: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)
overview: Diagnosis confirmed via Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3: oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries on ultrasound). Lifestyle intervention is first-line management for all presentations. Combined oral contraceptives are first-line pharmacological treatment for irregular cycles and hirsutism. Metformin is recommended for metabolic features and glycemic control (SMD -0.45 on BMI/insulin). Letrozole is first-line ovulation induction agent over Clomiphene (NEJM PPCOS II).
patient_plain_language: PCOS is a hormonal imbalance that affects how ovaries develop and release eggs, often linked to insulin resistance, causing irregular periods, acne, and excess hair growth.

name: Adult Persistent Asthma
overview: GINA Track 1 establishes low-dose ICS-Formoterol as the preferred reliever across all asthma severities. SYGMA 1 and 2 trials (NEJM 2018) proved as-needed ICS-Formoterol reduces severe exacerbations by 60-64% compared to SABA-only therapy, while reducing steroid exposure by 75-83%. SABA monotherapy is strongly discouraged due to increased risk of airway hyperresponsiveness and death.
patient_plain_language: Asthma is chronic inflammation of your airways that makes them swollen, sensitive, and tight when irritated. Using a rescue inhaler that contains both a muscle relaxer and a gentle anti-inflammatory calms the swelling instantly.

symptoms.name: Tachypnea and fatigue
symptoms.description: Elevated respiratory rate and physical tiredness. Characteristically observed in Adult Persistent Asthma.

name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
overview: ETHOS trial (n=8,509) demonstrated single-inhaler triple therapy (ICS/LAMA/LABA) significantly reduced the rate of moderate or severe COPD exacerbations by 24% compared to LAMA/LABA dual therapy (p<0.001) and reduced all-cause mortality by 46% in patients with blood eosinophil counts ≥100 cells/μL and history of exacerbations.

name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP)
overview: Clinical guideline establishes CURB-65 or Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) to determine outpatient vs. inpatient site of care. For healthy outpatients without comorbidities, monotherapy with Amoxicillin (1 g TID) or Doxycycline is strongly recommended over macrolides due to widespread pneumococcal resistance. For patients with comorbidities, combination therapy (beta-lactam + macrolide) or respiratory fluoroquinolones is recommended.

name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA)
overview: Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) is the gold standard therapy (AASM Grade Strong). Meta-analyses demonstrate CPAP reduces the Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI), decreases daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale score reduction by 2.5-3.0 points), and lowers 24-hour mean blood pressure by 2.0-2.5 mmHg, especially in resistant hypertension.

name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
overview: DAPA-CKD trial (n=4,304) demonstrated that in patients with eGFR 25-75 mL/min/1.73m² and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR) 200-5000 mg/g, Dapagliflozin reduced the composite risk of sustained ≥50% eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, or renal/CV death by 39% (HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.51-0.72; p<0.001). Benefits were consistent in non-diabetic CKD.
patient_plain_language: Chronic kidney disease means your kidneys' microscopic filtering units are gradually scarred, reducing their ability to clean waste and excess fluid from your blood.

name: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH)
overview: AUA guidelines recommend alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists (Tamsulosin, Alfuzosin) for rapid relief of lower urinary tract symptoms (IPSS improvement 4-6 points). 5-alpha reductase inhibitors (Finasteride, Dutasteride) are indicated for enlarged prostates (>30 cc), reducing prostate volume by ~25% and long-term risk of acute urinary retention and surgery by 50% (MTOPS Trial, NEJM).

name: Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infection (Cystitis)
overview: First-line empirical treatments with minimal resistance and collateral damage: Nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals (100 mg BID for 5 days), Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (160/800 mg BID for 3 days if local resistance <20%), or Fosfomycin trometamol (3 g single dose). Fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin) must be avoided for uncomplicated cystitis due to disabling adverse events and resistance.

name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD)
overview: Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) are the most effective therapy for erosive esophagitis healing (healing rates >80-90% vs. 50% with H2RAs). Guidelines recommend an 8-week course of once-daily PPI taken 30-60 minutes before the first meal of the day. Routine long-term high-dose therapy without objective confirmation or severe erosive disease is discouraged; deprescribing trials to the lowest effective dose are recommended.
patient_plain_language: Acid reflux occurs when the muscular valve between your food pipe and stomach doesn't close tightly, allowing harsh stomach acid to splash back up into the sensitive esophagus.

name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
overview: Diagnosis based on Rome IV criteria (recurrent abdominal pain ≥1 day/week associated with defecation or change in stool frequency/appearance). High-quality evidence supports soluble fiber (psyllium) over insoluble fiber (bran) (RR 0.79 for symptom persistence). A limited-time Low-FODMAP diet trial improves global symptoms (Grade conditional). Gut-directed hypnotherapy and neuromodulators (TCAs) exhibit strong NNT (NNT=4) for pain reduction via gut-brain axis modulation.
patient_plain_language: IBS is a disorder of the gut-brain connection where your intestines have become hypersensitive, causing abdominal cramping, bloating, diarrhea, or constipation without visible tissue damage.

name: Helicobacter pylori Infection
overview: Due to clarithromycin resistance exceeding 15-20% globally, 14-day Bismuth Quadruple Therapy (PPI + Bismuth subsalicylate + Metronidazole + Tetracycline) is the first-line treatment regimen, achieving eradication rates >85-90%. Clarithromycin triple therapy is now restricted only to regions with proven local resistance <15%. Eradication significantly reduces peptic ulcer recurrence and gastric cancer risk.

name: Celiac Disease
overview: Primary diagnosis requires serologic IgA tissue transglutaminase (tTG-IgA) testing with concurrent total IgA levels to rule out IgA deficiency. Confirmation in adults requires duodenal biopsy demonstrating intraepithelial lymphocytosis and villous atrophy (Marsh criteria). The only proven treatment is strict, lifelong adherence to a gluten-free diet (GFD), resulting in histological mucosal healing and prevention of lymphoma.
patient_plain_language: Celiac disease is an autoimmune condition where eating gluten (a protein in wheat, rye, and barley) triggers your immune system to attack and flatten the tiny finger-like villi in your small intestine that absorb nutrients.

name: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD)
overview: Analysis of 522 RCTs (n=116,477) established that all 21 antidepressants were more effective than placebo (ORs 1.37 to 2.13). Escitalopram, Sertraline, Vortioxetine, and Agomelatine showed favorable balance of high response rates and lowest discontinuation rates. name: Chronic Migraine
overview: Defined as ≥15 headache days/month for >3 months, with ≥8 days meeting migraine criteria. Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide (CGRP) monoclonal antibodies (Erenumab, Fremanezumab, Galcanezumab) and OnabotulinumtoxinA significantly reduce monthly migraine days by 4-6 days (NNT=3-4). Acute therapy relies on triptans or gepants. Limiting acute medications is essential to prevent medication-overuse headache (MOH).
patient_plain_language: Migraine is not just a bad headache; it is a neurological event where waves of nerve sensitivity and swelling around blood vessels in your brain cause throbbing pain, nausea, and light sensitivity.

name: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)
overview: Guidelines strongly advocate a 'Treat-to-Target' strategy aiming for clinical remission or low disease activity. Methotrexate monotherapy is strongly recommended as first-line conventional synthetic DMARD over other csDMARDs or biologics. If disease activity remains moderate or high despite optimized oral/subcutaneous MTX, adding a biologic DMARD (TNF inhibitor) or targeted synthetic DMARD is recommended.
patient_plain_language: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition where your immune system mistakenly attacks the lining of your joints (synovium), causing painful swelling that can damage bone over time if not calmed.

name: Chronic Non-Specific Lower Back Pain
overview: ACP guidelines recommend that clinicians and patients initially select nonpharmacological treatment with exercise, multidisciplinary rehabilitation, acupuncture, mindfulness-based stress reduction, or spinal manipulation (Grade: strong recommendation). name: Postmenopausal Osteoporosis
overview: Guidelines recommend initial treatment with oral bisphosphonates (Alendronate, Risedronate) or IV Zoledronic acid for postmenopausal women at high risk of fractures, reducing vertebral fractures by ~50-70% and hip fractures by ~40% (FIT and HORIZON trials). In women at very high risk (T-score <-3.0 or prior fracture), an anabolic regimen (Teriparatide, Romosozumab) followed by antiresorptive therapy is recommended.
patient_plain_language: Osteoporosis is a silent thinning of your bones where bone tissue breaks down faster than it rebuilds, making your bones porous like a sponge and more vulnerable to fractures from minor falls.

name: Menopausal Vasomotor Symptoms & Hormone Therapy
overview: Systemic hormone therapy is the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and the genitourinary syndrome of menopause. In women aged <60 years or within 10 years of menopause onset, the benefit-risk ratio is favorable for relief of hot flashes and fracture prevention without increased all-cause mortality. Women with an intact uterus require concurrent progestogen (e.g., micronized progesterone) to prevent endometrial cancer.
patient_plain_language: During perimenopause and menopause, your ovaries produce less estrogen, causing your brain's temperature control center to misfire and trigger sudden hot flashes and night sweats.

name: Endometriosis & Chronic Pelvic Pain
overview: ESHRE guidelines recommend empirical medical treatment without requiring laparoscopic confirmation in patients with clinical suspicion. Combined oral contraceptives or progestogens (Dienogest 2 mg) are first-line hormonal therapies (Grade A). GnRH receptor antagonists (Elagolix, Relugolix; ELARIS trials, NEJM) significantly reduce dysmenorrhea and non-menstrual pelvic pain with add-back therapy to preserve bone density.
patient_plain_language: Endometriosis occurs when tissue similar to the lining inside your uterus grows outside the womb on other pelvic organs, causing inflammation, scarring, and severe menstrual pain.

name: Preeclampsia Prevention & Management
overview: The USPSTF and ACOG recommend low-dose aspirin (81-150 mg/day) prophylaxis initiated between 12 and 16 weeks of gestation (and continued until delivery) in pregnant individuals at high risk for preeclampsia (Grade B). Meta-analyses (ASPRE trial, NEJM) confirm low-dose aspirin reduces preterm preeclampsia by ~62% and intrauterine growth restriction by ~20%.
patient_plain_language: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy complication characterized by high blood pressure and signs of strain on other organs like kidneys and liver, typically appearing after 20 weeks of pregnancy.

name: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM)
overview: HAPO study demonstrated strong, continuous linear associations between maternal glucose levels and adverse outcomes (birth weight >90th percentile, primary cesarean delivery, and neonatal hypoglycemia). First-line management is medical nutrition therapy and moderate exercise, which successfully manages 70-85% of GDM pregnancies. Insulin is the preferred first-line pharmacological treatment when glycemic goals are not met.
patient_plain_language: Gestational diabetes is temporary high blood sugar that develops during pregnancy because placental hormones interfere with how your body uses its own insulin.

name: Pediatric Acute Otitis Media (AOM)

patient_plain_language: An ear infection is inflammation and fluid trapped behind your child's eardrum, usually triggered by swelling from a common cold. Many mild ear infections resolve naturally with pain medicine.

name: Pediatric Asthma & Viral Wheeze

name: Simple Febrile Seizures
overview: Simple febrile seizures (generalized, lasting <15 minutes, occurring once in 24 hours in a child aged 6-60 months) carry no increased risk of long-term neurological damage, intellectual disability, or significant epilepsy risk compared to the general population. name: COVID-19 Acute Outpatient Management
overview: In nonhospitalized high-risk adult outpatients, oral Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir (Paxlovid) initiated within 5 days of symptom onset reduced COVID-19-related hospitalization or death by 89% compared to placebo (0.77% vs 6.31%; p<0.001). IV Remdesivir for 3 days represents an alternative high-efficacy antiviral option (PINETREE trial, 87% reduction). Concomitant drug interaction check is mandatory due to strong CYP3A4 inhibition by ritonavir.
patient_plain_language: COVID-19 is a viral respiratory infection that can cause severe lung inflammation in high-risk individuals. Antiviral pills work by stopping the virus from copying itself inside your cells, but must be started in the first few days of sickness.

name: Atopic Dermatitis (Eczema)
overview: AAD guidelines emphasize basic barrier repair with bland emollient ointments as foundational therapy. Topical corticosteroids (TCS) are first-line prescription therapy for flares. Topical calcineurin inhibitors (Tacrolimus) and PDE-4 inhibitors (Crisaborole) are recommended for sensitive areas (face, neck, skin folds). For moderate-to-severe disease refractory to topicals, biologic therapy with Dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα; LIBERTY AD trials, NEJM) provides significant clearance with an excellent safety profile.
patient_plain_language: Eczema is a condition where your skin's outer moisture barrier is leaky and easily inflamed, allowing water to escape and irritants to enter, causing intensely itchy, red, cracked patches.

name: Plaque Psoriasis
overview: For localized disease (<3% body surface area), high-potency topical corticosteroids combined with vitamin D analogues (Calcipotriene) are first-line. For moderate-to-severe disease (≥3-5% BSA or sensitive areas), targeted biologics (anti-IL-23: Risankizumab, Guselkumab; anti-IL-17: Secukinumab, Ixekizumab; anti-TNF: Adalimumab) achieve PASI 90 or PASI 100 skin clearance rates in 70-85% of patients (Phase 3 trials, NEJM/Lancet).

name: Cellulitis & Purulent Skin Infections
overview: IDSA guidelines classify SSTIs into purulent (abscess, furuncle) and non-purulent (cellulitis, erysipelas). For non-purulent cellulitis, beta-lactam monotherapy covering Streptococcus (Cephalexin or Cefazolin) is recommended (5-day course proven equivalent to 10 days in JAMA RCT). For purulent infections, incision and drainage is the primary therapy; empirical CA-MRSA antibiotic coverage (Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or Doxycycline) is added for systemic signs.

name: Early Localized Lyme Disease
overview: Patients with characteristic erythema migrans (EM) rash and history of potential tick exposure in an endemic area should be diagnosed and treated clinically without serologic testing (serology is insensitive in early localized disease, <40%). Oral Doxycycline (100 mg BID for 10-14 days) is first-line treatment. Single-dose prophylactic Doxycycline (200 mg) is recommended within 72 hours of removing an attached Ixodes scapularis tick after ≥36 hours of attachment.

name: Colorectal Cancer Screening
overview: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years (Grade A). Multiple screening strategies demonstrate strong mortality reduction: Colonoscopy every 10 years, annual Fecal Immunochemical Test (FIT), or stool DNA-FIT (Cologuard) every 3 years. Any positive non-invasive stool test mandates follow-up diagnostic colonoscopy.
patient_plain_language: Colorectal cancer screening checks for precancerous polyps (small growths on the inner colon wall) and removes them before they ever have the chance to transform into cancer.

name: Breast Cancer Screening
overview: The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years (Grade B). Collaborative modeling indicates that starting screening at age 40 rather than age 50 averts an additional 1.3 breast cancer deaths per 1,000 women screened, with favorable benefit-to-harm ratios regarding false-positive mammograms and benign biopsies.
patient_plain_language: A screening mammogram is a low-dose X-ray picture of the breast used to detect tiny changes or early tumors long before they can ever be felt with a hand.

name: Lung Cancer Screening
overview: The USPSTF recommends annual screening for lung cancer with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years (Grade B). The National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) demonstrated a 20% relative reduction in lung cancer mortality with LDCT compared to chest radiography.
patient_plain_language: Low-dose CT lung screening uses a quick, low-radiation scanner to take detailed cross-section images of your lungs to catch early-stage lung nodules when they are most curable.

name: Cervical Cancer Screening & HPV Triage
overview: USPSTF recommends screening for cervical cancer in women aged 21 to 65 years. Strategies: Cervical cytology (Pap smear) alone every 3 years for ages 21-29; for ages 30-65, options include high-risk HPV (hrHPV) testing alone every 5 years, hrHPV co-testing with cytology every 5 years, or cytology alone every 3 years. Primary hrHPV testing demonstrates superior sensitivity for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3+ (CIN 3+).
patient_plain_language: Cervical cancer screening checks the cells of your cervix for high-risk strains of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) that can cause cell changes years before cervical cancer could develop.

name: Crohn's Disease (Inflammatory Bowel Disease)
overview: Guidelines recommend a 'Treat-to-Target' strategy aiming for deep mucosal healing, not just symptom resolution. For moderate-to-severe disease, anti-TNF biologics (Infliximab, Adalimumab) or anti-integrins (Vedolizumab) are first-line to induce and maintain remission. Systemic corticosteroids should be used strictly for acute flares and never for maintenance due to severe long-term toxicity.
patient_plain_language: Crohn's disease is an autoimmune condition where your immune system attacks the lining of your digestive tract, causing deep ulcers, swelling, and scar tissue anywhere from the mouth to the colon.

name: Ulcerative Colitis (Inflammatory Bowel Disease)
overview: Unlike Crohn's, UC is limited to the mucosal layer of the colon. For mild-to-moderate UC, topical (rectal) and oral 5-aminosalicylates (5-ASA/Mesalamine) are first-line. For moderate-to-severe disease, targeted biologics (Infliximab, Vedolizumab) or JAK inhibitors (Tofacitinib) are recommended. Annual surveillance colonoscopy is required after 8 years of disease due to significantly elevated colorectal cancer risk.
patient_plain_language: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that causes continuous superficial sores (ulcers) specifically along the inner lining of your large intestine and rectum, leading to bloody diarrhea.

name: Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD)
overview: Diagnosis is established by a resting Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) ≤0.90. First-line therapy for intermittent claudication is Supervised Exercise Therapy (SET), which increases maximal walking distance by 100-150% (superior to pharmacotherapy). Antiplatelet therapy (Aspirin or Clopidogrel) and high-intensity statin therapy are mandatory to reduce the high risk of myocardial infarction and stroke in PAD patients.
patient_plain_language: Peripheral artery disease is caused by cholesterol plaque building up in the arteries of your legs, reducing blood flow. This causes your leg muscles to cramp and ache when walking because they are starved of oxygen.

name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
overview: Hydroxychloroquine is recommended for all patients with SLE, unless contraindicated, as it improves survival, reduces flares, and prevents organ damage (Grade A). Glucocorticoids should be used at the lowest possible dose (target ≤7.5 mg/day of prednisone) and tapered as soon as possible. Belimumab (anti-BAFF) is approved for autoantibody-positive SLE with inadequate response to standard therapy.

name: HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)
overview: Daily oral TDF/FTC (Truvada) or TAF/FTC (Descovy) reduces the risk of getting HIV from sex by about 99% when taken consistently. Long-acting injectable Cabotegravir (Apretude) given every 2 months was shown in HPTN 083/084 trials to be superior to daily oral PrEP in preventing HIV acquisition, offering an option for those with adherence challenges.

name: Chronic Hepatitis C (HCV)
overview: Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) such as Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir (Epclusa) or Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir (Mavyret) achieve Sustained Virologic Response (SVR) — considered a virologic cure — in >95% of patients across all genotypes after 8 to 12 weeks of oral therapy. Treatment is recommended for all patients with chronic HCV infection, except those with short life expectancies.
patient_plain_language: Hepatitis C is a viral infection that slowly damages the liver over decades. Modern antiviral pills can completely cure the infection in 8 to 12 weeks, stopping further liver damage.

name: Sickle Cell Disease
overview: Hydroxyurea is the primary disease-modifying therapy, strongly recommended for adults with ≥3 moderate-to-severe pain crises per year, demonstrating significant reductions in vaso-occlusive crises, acute chest syndrome, and mortality. name: Multiple Sclerosis (Relapsing-Remitting)
overview: In relapsing MS, high-efficacy Disease Modifying Therapies (DMTs) like Ocrelizumab (anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody) demonstrate superior efficacy over older therapies (Interferon beta-1a), lowering annualized relapse rates by 46% and significantly reducing disability progression. name: Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia (Jaundice)
overview: The AAP provides age-in-hours specific nomograms for initiating phototherapy or exchange transfusion. Universal screening of Total Serum Bilirubin (TSB) or Transcutaneous Bilirubin (TcB) is recommended before hospital discharge. Phototherapy is highly effective at converting unconjugated bilirubin into water-soluble isomers for excretion, preventing bilirubin encephalopathy (kernicterus).
patient_plain_language: Jaundice is a common, temporary yellowing of a newborn's skin and eyes caused by a buildup of bilirubin, a yellow pigment created as the baby breaks down extra red blood cells faster than their immature liver can process.

name: Acute Pancreatitis
overview: Aggressive early intravenous hydration (250-500 mL/hr of lactated Ringer's) within the first 12-24 hours is most beneficial to prevent tissue necrosis. Routine use of prophylactic antibiotics in severe acute pancreatitis is strongly discouraged. Early oral feeding (within 24 hours) with a low-fat solid diet is recommended over prolonged fasting (NPO) to protect the gut mucosal barrier.
patient_plain_language: Acute pancreatitis is a sudden, severe inflammation where the digestive enzymes made by the pancreas become activated too early, essentially digesting the pancreas itself and causing intense abdominal pain.

name: Cirrhosis & Portal Hypertension
overview: Non-selective beta-blockers (NSBBs: Propranolol, Nadolol, Carvedilol) or Endoscopic Band Ligation (EBL) are recommended for primary prophylaxis of medium-to-large esophageal varices to prevent catastrophic bleeding. NSBBs lower portal pressure by decreasing cardiac output and causing splanchnic vasoconstriction. Diuretics (Spironolactone + Furosemide ratio 100:40) remain first-line for ascites management.
patient_plain_language: Cirrhosis is severe scarring of the liver that blocks normal blood flow. This causes pressure to back up into the veins of your stomach and esophagus (portal hypertension), and fluid to leak into your belly (ascites).

name: Acute Ischemic Stroke
overview: Intravenous Tenecteplase or Alteplase (tPA) is strongly recommended for eligible patients presenting within 3.0 to 4.5 hours of symptom onset. Mechanical thrombectomy is the standard of care for large vessel occlusions (LVO) in the anterior circulation within 24 hours of last known normal, provided the patient meets specific clinical/imaging mismatch criteria (DAWN and DEFUSE-3 trials).
patient_plain_language: An ischemic stroke happens when a blood clot blocks a blood vessel in the brain, cutting off oxygen. Brain cells die rapidly, so emergency clot-busting medicine or surgical clot removal must happen within hours.

symptoms.name: Headache / Cranial pain
symptoms.description: Recurrent or progressive head discomfort or throbbing. Characteristically observed in Acute Ischemic Stroke.

symptoms.name: Dizziness and balance impairment

symptoms.name: Cognitive changes / Memory lapses

symptoms.name: Sensory paresthesias / Numbness
symptoms.description: Tingling, prickling, or decreased sensation in extremities. Characteristically observed in Acute Ischemic Stroke.

symptoms.name: Tremors or motor weakness
symptoms.description: Involuntary shaking or localized muscle weakness. Characteristically observed in Acute Ischemic Stroke.

red_flags: F.A.S.T: Sudden Facial drooping, Arm weakness, or Speech difficulty (Call 911 immediately)

name: Adult Epilepsy & Seizure Disorders
overview: Levetiracetam, Lamotrigine, and Zonisamide demonstrate Level A evidence for new-onset focal epilepsy in adults. Valproic acid remains highly effective for generalized epilepsy but carries severe teratogenic risks and is contraindicated in women of childbearing potential without strict contraception. Over 60-70% of patients achieve seizure freedom on monotherapy.
patient_plain_language: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder where clusters of nerve cells in the brain sometimes signal abnormally, causing a sudden surge of electrical activity that results in a seizure.

name: Bipolar I Disorder
overview: First-line agents for acute mania include Lithium, Quetiapine, Divalproex, Asenapine, and Aripiprazole. For bipolar depression, Quetiapine, Lurasidone, and Lithium are first-line. Antidepressants (SSRIs/SNRIs) must be avoided as monotherapy in Bipolar I due to the high risk of triggering manic switching or rapid cycling.
patient_plain_language: Bipolar disorder is a brain condition that causes extreme, uncontrollable shifts in mood, energy, and activity levels, ranging from deep depressions to euphoric or irritable 'manic' highs.

symptoms.name: Psychomotor and autonomic symptoms
symptoms.description: Restlessness, tremors, diaphoresis, or muscle tension. Characteristically observed in Bipolar I Disorder.

name: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)
overview: Trauma-focused psychotherapies (Prolonged Exposure [PE], Cognitive Processing Therapy [CPT], and EMDR) have the strongest evidence base and are recommended over pharmacotherapy as first-line interventions (Grade A). name: Sepsis & Septic Shock
overview: The 'Hour-1 Bundle' is critical for mortality reduction: 1) Measure lactate, 2) Obtain blood cultures before antibiotics, 3) Administer broad-spectrum IV antibiotics, 4) Begin rapid 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid fluid resuscitation for hypotension or lactate ≥4 mmol/L, 5) Apply vasopressors (Norepinephrine first-line) if hypotensive during/after fluids. Every hour delay in antibiotics increases mortality.
patient_plain_language: Sepsis is a life-threatening emergency where the body's immune system overreacts to an infection, causing widespread inflammation that damages tissues, drops blood pressure, and shuts down organs.

symptoms.name: Fever and chills / Rigors

symptoms.name: Generalized malaise and fatigue

symptoms.name: Localized erythema, pain, or purulence
symptoms.description: Focal signs of infection at specific anatomical site. Characteristically observed in Sepsis & Septic Shock.

symptoms.name: Lymphadenopathy
symptoms.description: Enlarged, tender regional lymph nodes. Characteristically observed in Sepsis & Septic Shock.

red_flags: Extreme shivering, muscle pain, no urine output all day, severe breathlessness, and mottled/discolored skin (Medical Emergency)

name: Active Tuberculosis (TB)
overview: Standard treatment for drug-susceptible active TB requires a 4-drug intensive phase for 2 months (Isoniazid [INH], Rifampin [RIF], Pyrazinamide [PZA], Ethambutol [EMB]), followed by a 2-drug continuation phase for 4 months (INH and RIF). patient_plain_language: Tuberculosis is a serious bacterial infection that usually attacks the lungs. It requires a long, uninterrupted course of multiple antibiotics over 6 months to completely kill the tough bacteria and prevent it from mutating.

name: Syphilis
overview: Parenteral Penicillin G is the only therapy with documented efficacy across all stages of syphilis. Primary, secondary, and early latent syphilis require a single dose of Benzathine penicillin G (2.4 million units IM). Late latent or unknown duration requires 3 doses spaced 1 week apart. Neurosyphilis requires aqueous crystalline penicillin G IV for 10-14 days. Doxycycline is an alternative for penicillin-allergic non-pregnant patients.
patient_plain_language: Syphilis is a bacterial infection typically spread by sexual contact that progresses in stages. If treated early with a specific penicillin injection, it is easily cured, but left untreated, it can permanently damage the brain and heart.

name: Hyperthyroidism & Graves' Disease
overview: Methimazole (MMI) is the preferred first-line antithyroid drug over Propylthiouracil (PTU) due to PTU's risk of severe hepatotoxicity (except during the first trimester of pregnancy where PTU is preferred). Beta-blockers (e.g., Atenolol, Propranolol) are strongly recommended for symptomatic control of palpitations and tremors. Radioactive iodine or thyroidectomy are definitive treatments if medications fail or are contraindicated.
patient_plain_language: Graves' disease is an autoimmune condition where antibodies act like a broken thermostat, telling your thyroid gland to constantly pump out hormones, making your metabolism race out of control.

symptoms.name: Unexplained weight changes

symptoms.name: Chronic fatigue and lethargy

symptoms.name: Polydipsia / Polyuria

symptoms.name: Thermal intolerance (Heat/Cold)
symptoms.description: Abnormal sensitivity to cold or warm ambient temperatures. Characteristically observed in Hyperthyroidism & Graves' Disease.

symptoms.name: Mood and sleep disturbances
symptoms.description: Irritability, anxiety, or disrupted nocturnal sleep. Characteristically observed in Hyperthyroidism & Graves' Disease.

red_flags: Sudden severe fever, rapid heart rate >140 bpm, confusion, and agitation (Thyroid Storm: Medical Emergency)

name: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI)
overview: AKI is defined by an increase in serum creatinine by ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours, or ≥1.5x baseline within 7 days, or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/hr for 6 hours. Management is strictly driven by the cause (Pre-renal, Intrinsic, Post-renal). Rapid IV crystalloid volume expansion is required for hypovolemic pre-renal AKI. Nephrotoxic medications (NSAIDs, ACEi/ARBs, contrast) must be immediately discontinued.
patient_plain_language: Acute kidney injury is a sudden drop in kidney function, often caused by severe dehydration, toxic medications, or a blockage, which prevents the kidneys from filtering toxins and making urine.

symptoms.name: Peripheral and facial edema
symptoms.description: Fluid retention in periorbital tissue, pretibial, and ankles. Characteristically observed in Acute Kidney Injury (AKI).

symptoms.name: Urinary alterations (Frothy / Dark / Dysuria)
symptoms.description: Changes in urine color, foaminess, or frequency. Characteristically observed in Acute Kidney Injury (AKI).

symptoms.name: Fatigue and anemia-related weakness
symptoms.description: Due to reduced erythropoietin and uremic toxin buildup. Characteristically observed in Acute Kidney Injury (AKI).

symptoms.name: Hypertension
symptoms.description: Volume overload and hyperreninemia driving elevated blood pressure. Characteristically observed in Acute Kidney Injury (AKI).

symptoms.name: Pruritus and metallic taste
symptoms.description: Uremic symptoms in advanced renal compromise. Characteristically observed in Acute Kidney Injury (AKI).

red_flags: Complete cessation of urine output for over 12 hours
Severe shortness of breath, confusion, and nausea (Uremic syndrome or fluid in lungs)

name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF)
overview: Antifibrotic medications, Nintedanib (tyrosine kinase inhibitor) and Pirfenidone, are strongly recommended as they significantly slow the rate of Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) decline by approximately 50% (INPULSIS and ASCEND trials). Corticosteroids combined with immunosuppressants (azathioprine) are strongly recommended AGAINST, as they increase mortality and hospitalizations in IPF.
patient_plain_language: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is a progressive disease where the delicate air sacs in the lungs become thick, stiff, and scarred like a dried sponge, making it difficult for oxygen to enter the bloodstream.

name: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
alternative_names: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
overview: In the EMPEROR-Preserved trial, Empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) reduced the combined risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure by 21% (HR 0.79; p<0.001) in patients with LVEF >40%. SGLT2 inhibitors (Empagliflozin, Dapagliflozin) are now the first proven disease-modifying therapy for HFpEF and are Class 2a recommendations in AHA/ACC guidelines. Loop diuretics (Furosemide) remain essential for symptom relief of congestion.
patient_plain_language: In HFpEF (diastolic heart failure), your heart pumps with normal strength, but the heart muscle is too stiff to relax and fill with enough blood between beats, causing fluid to back up into the lungs and legs.

symptoms.name: Chest tightness / discomfort
symptoms.description: Pressure or constriction across anterior precordium. Characteristically observed in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF).

symptoms.name: Exertional dyspnea
symptoms.description: Shortness of breath on physical exertion. Characteristically observed in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF).

symptoms.name: Lower extremity peripheral edema
symptoms.description: Dependent fluid accumulation in ankles and feet. Characteristically observed in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF).

symptoms.name: Palpitations / Irregular heartbeat
symptoms.description: Sensation of rapid or skipping heart beats. Characteristically observed in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF).

symptoms.name: Fatigue and reduced stamina
symptoms.description: Generalized reduction in exercise capacity. Characteristically observed in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF).

red_flags: Waking up gasping for air in the middle of the night (Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea)

name: Fibromyalgia
overview: Non-pharmacological therapies (specifically graded aerobic exercise) have the highest evidence level (Grade A) and are the only universally recommended first-line therapy. Pharmacotherapy is tailored to specific symptoms: Duloxetine or Milnacipran (SNRIs) for depression/pain; Pregabalin for sleep/pain. name: Gallstone Disease (Cholelithiasis & Cholecystitis)
overview: Asymptomatic gallstones should generally not be treated or followed (except in specific high-risk populations). For symptomatic biliary colic, laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the definitive treatment. In cases of acute cholecystitis, early laparoscopic cholecystectomy (within 72 hours of admission) is superior to delayed surgery, reducing hospital stay and complications. name: Schizophrenia
overview: Second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs: e.g., Risperidone, Olanzapine, Aripiprazole) are first-line for acute exacerbations and maintenance. Clozapine is strictly indicated for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (failure of 2 adequate antipsychotic trials) or patients with high suicide risk, due to risk of severe agranulocytosis. name: Chronic Venous Insufficiency (CVI) & Varicose Veins
overview: Compression therapy (20-30 mmHg graduated compression stockings) is the primary conservative treatment to reduce edema and pain, and is mandatory to promote the healing of venous stasis ulcers (Grade 1B). name: Anaphylaxis
overview: Epinephrine (intramuscular into the anterolateral thigh) is the only first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. Antihistamines (H1/H2 blockers) and corticosteroids are second-line adjunctive therapies that do not treat the life-threatening respiratory or cardiovascular compromise of anaphylaxis and must never delay epinephrine administration. A second dose of epinephrine may be required in 5-15 minutes if symptoms do not improve.

name: Acute Diverticulitis
overview: For acute uncomplicated diverticulitis in immunocompetent patients, routine use of antibiotics is no longer recommended, as RCTs show no improvement in recovery time or prevention of complications (Grade: Conditional). Management relies on clear liquid diet and pain control. Antibiotics (e.g., Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole) are reserved for complicated cases (abscess, perforation) or high-risk patients.
patient_plain_language: Diverticulitis happens when small, bulging pouches in the lining of your large intestine become inflamed or infected, usually causing severe pain in the lower left side of the belly.

name: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis)
overview: GCA is a medical emergency due to the high risk of irreversible blindness. High-dose systemic glucocorticoids (Prednisone 40-60 mg/day; IV Methylprednisolone if visual symptoms are present) must be started immediately upon clinical suspicion, before biopsy confirmation. Tocilizumab (IL-6 receptor antagonist) combined with a steroid taper is strongly recommended over steroids alone to reduce cumulative steroid toxicity and flares.
patient_plain_language: Giant cell arteritis is severe inflammation of the blood vessels in your scalp, neck, and arms. If the inflammation blocks the artery supplying the eye, it can cause sudden, permanent blindness.

symptoms.name: Morning stiffness (>30-60 min)
symptoms.description: Severe difficulty moving joints upon waking. Characteristically observed in Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

symptoms.name: Joint swelling and erythema
symptoms.description: Synovial effusion, warmth, and periarticular soft tissue fullness. Characteristically observed in Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

symptoms.name: Decreased range of motion
symptoms.description: Reduced flexion/extension in affected joints. Characteristically observed in Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

symptoms.name: Systemic fatigue and malaise
symptoms.description: Persistent inflammatory physical exhaustion. Characteristically observed in Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).

red_flags: Sudden blurriness, double vision, or a dark curtain falling over the vision of one eye
Severe pain in the jaw muscles while chewing (Jaw Claudication)

name: Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma (POAG)
overview: Lowering intraocular pressure (IOP) is the only proven method to slow visual field loss. Topical prostaglandin analogs (Latanoprost, Bimatoprost) are the preferred first-line medical therapy due to once-daily dosing and high efficacy (lowering IOP by 25-33%). Selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) is equally effective as a first-line alternative to eye drops (LiGHT Trial, The Lancet).
patient_plain_language: Open-angle glaucoma is a slow, painless disease where fluid builds up inside the eye, raising the pressure and gradually damaging the optic nerve, slowly stealing your peripheral (side) vision.

symptoms.name: Sensory paresthesias / Numbness

symptoms.name: Tremors or motor weakness
symptoms.description: Involuntary shaking or localized muscle weakness. Characteristically observed in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma (POAG).

name: Age-Related Macular Degeneration (AMD)
overview: For intermediate dry AMD, AREDS2 antioxidant vitamin formulation (Vitamin C, E, Lutein, Zeaxanthin, Zinc, Copper) reduces the 5-year risk of progression to advanced AMD by 25%. For advanced 'wet' (neovascular) AMD, intravitreal anti-VEGF injections (Bevacizumab, Ranibizumab, Aflibercept) are the standard of care, preventing severe vision loss in over 90% of patients and improving vision in 30%.
patient_plain_language: Macular degeneration damages the macula—the center part of the retina responsible for sharp, straight-ahead vision needed for reading and recognizing faces. It does not cause complete darkness, but rather a blurry or missing spot in the center of your sight.

name: Bell's Palsy (Idiopathic Facial Paralysis)
overview: Oral corticosteroids (e.g., Prednisone 60 mg/day for 5 days, then tapered) initiated within 72 hours of symptom onset significantly increase the probability of complete facial nerve recovery (Grade A). The addition of antiviral therapy (valacyclovir) provides only modest, conditional benefit for severe cases (House-Brackmann grade V-VI) but should not be used as monotherapy.

name: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
overview: First-line conservative management includes neutral-angle wrist splinting (worn primarily at night) and local corticosteroid injections, which provide robust short-to-medium term relief (Grade Strong). Oral NSAIDs, diuretics, and gabapentin are not recommended. For patients with severe nerve compression (muscle atrophy) or those failing conservative therapy, surgical carpal tunnel release provides excellent long-term outcomes.
patient_plain_language: Carpal tunnel syndrome occurs when the median nerve is squeezed or compressed as it travels through a narrow passageway in your wrist, causing numbness, tingling, and weakness in your hand.

name: Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (Concussion)
overview: Routine neuroimaging (CT/MRI) is NOT recommended for mild TBI without red-flag symptoms, to avoid unnecessary radiation exposure (Grade A). name: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever)
overview: Intranasal corticosteroids (INCS: Fluticasone, Budesonide) are the most effective monotherapy for all symptoms of allergic rhinitis (sneezing, congestion, itching) and are strongly recommended as first-line treatment for moderate-to-severe disease. Oral second-generation antihistamines (Cetirizine, Loratadine) are effective for mild, episodic symptoms but do not relieve severe nasal congestion. First-generation antihistamines (Diphenhydramine) should be avoided due to sedation and anticholinergic side effects.
patient_plain_language: Allergic rhinitis occurs when your immune system overreacts to harmless particles like pollen or dust, causing inflammation, swelling, and mucus production in your nasal passages.

symptoms.name: Lymphadenopathy

red_flags: Unilateral (one-sided) nasal obstruction with blood-tinged discharge (Requires ENT evaluation to rule out polyps or masses)

name: Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (Hives)
overview: Defined as hives occurring most days for >6 weeks. First-line therapy is regular-dosed modern second-generation H1-antihistamines (Cetirizine, Fexofenadine). If symptoms persist after 2-4 weeks, guidelines strongly recommend increasing the antihistamine dose up to four-fold (Grade A). If refractory to high-dose antihistamines, Omalizumab (anti-IgE biologic) is the recommended add-on therapy.
patient_plain_language: Chronic hives are itchy, raised, red welts on the skin that come and go daily for more than 6 weeks, usually caused by an overactive immune system rather than a specific allergy to a food or chemical.

symptoms.name: Cutaneous erythema and rash
symptoms.description: Redness, papules, plaques, or macular lesions on skin. Characteristically observed in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (Hives).

symptoms.name: Severe pruritus (Itching)
symptoms.description: Intense urge to scratch causing secondary excoriation. Characteristically observed in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (Hives).

symptoms.name: Skin scaling and flaking
symptoms.description: Keratotic shedding or silvery/white scales on lesions. Characteristically observed in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (Hives).

symptoms.name: Skin xerosis (Dryness)
symptoms.description: Rough, cracked, or irritable skin barrier. Characteristically observed in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (Hives).

symptoms.name: Burning sensation or pain
symptoms.description: Stinging or localized tenderness across skin. Characteristically observed in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria (Hives).

red_flags: Hives accompanied by lip swelling, difficulty breathing, or dizziness (Anaphylaxis)

name: Acne Vulgaris
overview: Topical retinoids (Adapalene, Tretinoin) are the foundation of acne therapy, targeting microcomedone formation. Benzoyl peroxide should always be added when topical or oral antibiotics are used to prevent bacterial resistance. name: Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR)
overview: Low-dose systemic glucocorticoids (Prednisone 12.5-25 mg/day) are the cornerstone of therapy, providing dramatic and rapid symptom relief (often within 48-72 hours). Tapering should be slow and individualized (typically lasting 1-2 years) to prevent relapse. Methotrexate may be considered early in patients at high risk for steroid toxicity or those with relapsing disease.
patient_plain_language: Polymyalgia rheumatica is an inflammatory disorder causing widespread muscle aching and severe morning stiffness, primarily affecting the shoulders and hips in older adults. It responds exceptionally well to low-dose steroids.

symptoms.name: Joint pain (Arthralgia)

symptoms.name: Morning stiffness (>30-60 min)
symptoms.description: Severe difficulty moving joints upon waking. Characteristically observed in Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR).

symptoms.name: Joint swelling and erythema
symptoms.description: Synovial effusion, warmth, and periarticular soft tissue fullness. Characteristically observed in Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR).

symptoms.name: Decreased range of motion
symptoms.description: Reduced flexion/extension in affected joints. Characteristically observed in Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR).

symptoms.name: Systemic fatigue and malaise
symptoms.description: Persistent inflammatory physical exhaustion. Characteristically observed in Polymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR).

red_flags: New, severe, localized headache, jaw pain while chewing, or sudden vision changes (Indicates concurrent Giant Cell Arteritis emergency)

name: Thyroid Nodules
overview: The initial evaluation of a thyroid nodule requires measuring serum TSH. If TSH is subnormal (hyperthyroidism), a radionuclide thyroid scan is required (functioning 'hot' nodules are rarely malignant). If TSH is normal or elevated, a dedicated thyroid ultrasound determines the need for Fine-Needle Aspiration (FNA) biopsy based on sonographic pattern (e.g., solid, hypoechoic, microcalcifications) and size (typically >1 cm for high suspicion).
patient_plain_language: A thyroid nodule is a solid or fluid-filled lump within the thyroid gland in your neck. The vast majority are benign (non-cancerous), but ultrasound features and a simple needle biopsy are used to be absolutely sure.

symptoms.description: Abnormal sensitivity to cold or warm ambient temperatures. Characteristically observed in Thyroid Nodules.

symptoms.name: Mood and sleep disturbances
symptoms.description: Irritability, anxiety, or disrupted nocturnal sleep. Characteristically observed in Thyroid Nodules.

red_flags: Rapid growth of a firm, fixed nodule in the neck

name: Ectopic Pregnancy
overview: Diagnosis requires transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) and serial quantitative beta-hCG measurements. If a patient is hemodynamically stable, willing to comply with post-treatment follow-up, and meets criteria (mass <3-4 cm, no fetal cardiac activity), medical management with intramuscular Methotrexate is safe and effective. Hemodynamic instability or evidence of rupture mandates immediate surgical intervention (laparoscopy/salpingectomy).
patient_plain_language: An ectopic pregnancy occurs when a fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, most commonly in a fallopian tube. It cannot survive, and as it grows, it poses a life-threatening risk of rupturing the tube and causing severe internal bleeding.

name: Postmenopausal Bleeding & Endometrial Hyperplasia
overview: Any postmenopausal bleeding requires immediate investigation to rule out endometrial cancer (present in ~10% of cases). Initial evaluation options are transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) or endometrial biopsy. An endometrial thickness of ≤4 mm on TVUS carries a >99% negative predictive value for endometrial cancer, and observation is reasonable. Thickness >4 mm requires endometrial tissue sampling.

name: Erectile Dysfunction (ED)
overview: ED is a recognized early clinical marker for underlying Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (ASCVD); symptoms of ED often precede coronary events by 3-5 years. Phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitors (Sildenafil, Tadalafil) are first-line oral therapy. PDE5 inhibitors are absolutely contraindicated in patients taking nitrates (due to severe refractory hypotension) and must be used with caution with alpha-blockers.
patient_plain_language: Erectile dysfunction is often a plumbing issue caused by the same plaque buildup that causes heart disease. The tiny blood vessels in the penis become narrowed years before the larger arteries in the heart do.

symptoms.name: Chest tightness / discomfort

name: Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS)
overview: First-line evaluation must include checking serum ferritin, as brain iron deficiency is a primary driver of RLS. If ferritin is <75 ng/mL, iron supplementation is the first-line therapy. For pharmacological symptom control, alpha-2-delta ligands (Pregabalin, Gabapentin enacarbil) are preferred. Dopamine agonists (Pramipexole, Ropinirole) are effective but carry a high risk of 'augmentation' (paradoxical worsening of symptoms over time).
patient_plain_language: Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder causing an overwhelming, uncomfortable urge to move your legs, usually occurring in the evening or when trying to sleep, severely disrupting rest.

symptoms.name: Headache / Cranial pain
symptoms.description: Recurrent or progressive head discomfort or throbbing. Characteristically observed in Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS).

symptoms.name: Dizziness and balance impairment
symptoms.description: Unsteadiness, vertigo, or difficulty coordinating steps. Characteristically observed in Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS).

symptoms.name: Cognitive changes / Memory lapses
symptoms.description: Short-term recall deficit or mental fog. Characteristically observed in Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS).

symptoms.name: Sensory paresthesias / Numbness
symptoms.description: Tingling, prickling, or decreased sensation in extremities. Characteristically observed in Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS).

symptoms.name: Tremors or motor weakness
symptoms.description: Involuntary shaking or localized muscle weakness. Characteristically observed in Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS).

red_flags: Severe daytime sleepiness leading to falling asleep while driving

name: Acute Appendicitis
overview: Laparoscopic appendectomy remains the gold standard treatment for acute appendicitis. While non-operative management (antibiotics alone) can be successful in selected patients with uncomplicated appendicitis, there is a recurrence rate of up to 39% at 5 years (CODA trial). Surgery is mandatory for complicated appendicitis (perforation, peritonitis, abscess).
patient_plain_language: Appendicitis is a sudden infection and inflammation of the appendix, a small pouch attached to the large intestine. It typically requires quick surgical removal before it can burst.

symptoms.name: Abdominal pain or cramping
symptoms.description: Localized or diffuse visceral abdominal pain. Characteristically observed in Acute Appendicitis.

symptoms.name: Altered bowel habits (Diarrhea/Constipation)
symptoms.description: Change in stool frequency, consistency, or urgency. Characteristically observed in Acute Appendicitis.

symptoms.name: Nausea, dyspepsia, or vomiting
symptoms.description: Postprandial fullness, burning, or emesis. Characteristically observed in Acute Appendicitis.

symptoms.name: Bloating and abdominal distension
symptoms.description: Visible fullness or discomfort after meals. Characteristically observed in Acute Appendicitis.

symptoms.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding (Melena/Hematochezia)
symptoms.description: Blood in stool or darkened tarry bowel movements. Characteristically observed in Acute Appendicitis.

red_flags: Pain starting around the belly button that shifts to the lower right abdomen and becomes intense
Sudden relief of severe pain followed by a high fever and a rigid, swollen abdomen (Indicates the appendix has burst/perforated)

name: Hyperkalemia (Elevated Blood Potassium)
overview: Severe hyperkalemia (≥6.5 mEq/L) or any hyperkalemia with ECG changes (peaked T waves, widened QRS) is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate myocardial stabilization with IV Calcium Gluconate (or Calcium Chloride). This must be followed by intracellular potassium-shifting agents (IV Insulin with Dextrose, Albuterol) and eventually potassium-removing agents (Loop diuretics, GI cation binders like Patiromer, or emergent Hemodialysis).
patient_plain_language: Hyperkalemia is dangerously high potassium in the blood, usually because the kidneys cannot filter it out. Because potassium controls the heart's electrical rhythm, high levels can cause the heart to suddenly stop.

symptoms.name: Peripheral and facial edema
symptoms.description: Fluid retention in periorbital tissue, pretibial, and ankles. Characteristically observed in Hyperkalemia (Elevated Blood Potassium).

symptoms.name: Urinary alterations (Frothy / Dark / Dysuria)
symptoms.description: Changes in urine color, foaminess, or frequency. Characteristically observed in Hyperkalemia (Elevated Blood Potassium).

symptoms.name: Fatigue and anemia-related weakness
symptoms.description: Due to reduced erythropoietin and uremic toxin buildup. Characteristically observed in Hyperkalemia (Elevated Blood Potassium).

symptoms.name: Hypertension
symptoms.description: Volume overload and hyperreninemia driving elevated blood pressure. Characteristically observed in Hyperkalemia (Elevated Blood Potassium).

symptoms.name: Pruritus and metallic taste
symptoms.description: Uremic symptoms in advanced renal compromise. Characteristically observed in Hyperkalemia (Elevated Blood Potassium).

red_flags: Muscle weakness, numbness, or tingling in the limbs
Heart palpitations, skipped beats, or severe shortness of breath (Medical Emergency)
